core_job: A pivot that needs founder approval first. GadgetNest drops price comparison entirely. That job is FashionFactory's, it needs an unfunded retailer feed, and a release build today lists nothing (catalogProvider returns {} when pricesBlocked, app_state.dart:23-27). GadgetNest becomes a household security-update tracker. The person who looks after the family's devices lists every phone, tablet, watch and e-reader at home and sees when each one stops getting security updates, ordered by what runs out first, with a reminder before it happens. Data comes from endoflife.date (keyless, MIT). This session's curl checks of /api/v1/products and /api/v1/categories/device both returned HTTP 200, the latter listing 21 device products with real dates (e.g. Pixel 10 Pro eolFrom 2032-08-01). Where a maker publishes no end date, as Apple does, the app says exactly that and never guesses.
signature: The Support Clock. The app reads this phone's model name on-device (device_info_plus modelName) and checks it in one tap. Other devices come from a maker and model picker over live endoflife.date product files. Each device gets a sourced lifespan bar with a countdown and the maker's own wording ("Security Updates", "Supported", "End of Servicing Date"). Matching happens on the device, and the app downloads whole public files, so the device list is never sent anywhere. Local reminders fire 6 months and 30 days before end of support. When a maker extends support, the app shows the change ("was Jul 2030, now Jul 2032"). There is a Timeline view by end year, with "Ended" and "No announced end" lanes. In an App Store Search API scan (9 queries, 174 distinct apps, US), no description mentions per-device security-update end dates. Warranty and recall trackers are crowded (CoverKeep, Manifest and CoverlyAI already advertise recall alerts), so those stay out of the signature. Web search was disabled this session, so competitor claims rest only on the App Store API descriptions.
must: M1 Remove the dead commerce app: delete catalog/pricing/affiliate/models, the browse/deals/compare/product/saved/build_list features, the 3D carousel and tilt widgets, and the price widgets. Remove every --dart-define data switch (GADGETNEST_INVENTORY, ALLOW_SAMPLE_DATA, SUPPLIER_CONFIGURED, AFFILIATE_MARKER, SCREENSHOT/storeCapture) and every 'in this build' / 'not connected' / 'Live prices are unavailable' / 'Where prices come from' string. Replace the tests for removed code, and list each replacement in the commit.

M2 Support Clock end to end on a fresh install. An endoflife.date v1 client (15 s timeout) uses the per-maker labels. Status rules: a future eolFrom shows a countdown; within 12 months shows 'Ending soon'; isEol shows 'No longer gets security updates'; a null eolFrom shows 'maker does not announce an end date' (never estimated); hand-added gadgets show 'No public support data'. An on-device modelName matcher never auto-picks when the match is ambiguous. Source and maker policy link shown on each device.

M3 Household list as home, with depth. Persisted devices with nickname, person, purchase date and notes; edit and delete. Filters: person, ending within 12 months, ended. Search, and a 'runs out first' sort. A plain-text household report via the share sheet. First-run empty state with 'Check this iPhone' / 'Add a device'. Offline mode reads from a cache with a dated banner; with no cache, a Retry state; a malformed response falls back to the cache. Pull to refresh, plus an automatic refresh when the cache is older than 7 days.

M4 Local reminders at eolFrom minus 6 months and minus 30 days, 09:00 local time, never in the past, cancelled on delete. Notification permission is asked on the first toggle; inexact scheduling only. Change detection against lastKnown, with a badge and a history entry.

M5 Own identity. 'Circuit board' palette: bone #F4F3EE, ink #13221D, PCB green #1F4D3A, copper #B8652A, muted #5E6B66; status #2E7D5B / #C27C0E / #A63A2B; dark #0E1A16 / #E8ECE6. A grep found none of these ten hexes in any app or sibling spec. Red Hat Text for UI and Red Hat Mono for dates, bundled under the OFL, replacing Inter. 6 dp board-style cards with a lifespan bar. No bottom NavigationBar: a Timeline/List segmented home (Cupertino control on iOS) with a 'This phone' card. One-screen onboarding. Settings in the app's own words. A hand-drawn icon (phone outline with a copper countdown arc, no Material glyph or gradient), with the GadgetNest entry removed from generate_app_icons.py:69. Launch screen #F4F3EE, so it no longer hashes to 3f6a9b27d8. New pubspec description.
M6 Remove AppShell and the tab-change interstitial. One AglAdBanner at the bottom of the home list only; none on onboarding, picker, detail or Settings.

M7 Honest and 5.6-safe. Real data only: endoflife.date, the device's own model name, and what the user types. No sample household, no invented dates, no account or demo, no remote config reads, no reviewer/region/date detection, no hidden gestures. Every feature is reachable within two taps. Tests use real captured API responses stored as dated fixtures.

M8 Proven. flutter analyze clean; all tests pass. New tests cover parsing, status rules with an injected clock, the matcher, the reminder schedule, change detection, persistence/filter/search/sort, cache and offline, the export format, onboarding, a tell guard, and rewritten accessibility/foldable/layout tests. Screenshot integration test against the live API. Path-limited commits that never stage fastlane/ or ios/Podfile.lock (someone else has uncommitted edits to it). Launch on a simulator and look at the screens.
